newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Strike cripples work at Colombo port.
newsitem.headline: Strike cripples work at Colombo port.

text.p: A strike by union labour opposing government plans to lease part of Colombo port to a consortium led by the Peninsula & Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) crippled work at south Asia's trans-shipment hub on Friday.
A Ports and Shipping Ministry spokesman said only four of the port's 12 gantry cranes were working at the Jaye Container Terminal (JCT) two and JCT three.
Labour unions which organised the strike to protest against plans to lease the Queen Elizabeth Quay said most of their members among the port's 14,000-strong work force stayed away.
The port's container and break bulk cargo terminals, usually bustling with workers, were deserted on Friday morning.
The ministry spokesman said striking workers initially prevented those who came to work from entering the harbour.
"But now they are being allowed to enter," he said. "We're working two container vessels at the JCT while the Queen Elizabeth Quay handled two ships in the morning."
Labour unions say they oppose the P&O deal as they fear it will lead to retrenchment and losses to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), which runs Colombo port.
The SLPA is currently holding talks with P&O to turn Queen Elizabeth Quay into a new container terminal to expand capacity and later build a new port adjacent to the present one.

The project, estimated to cost up to one billion dollars and take 10 years to build, will see the development of the southern part of the port with at least another six deep-draft berths, with a capacity of two million containers per year.
Ports and Shipping Minister Mohamed Ashraff told labour union leaders on Thursday he would only go ahead with the deal if it was profitable.
Ashraff urged workers not to damage the port's reputation by striking, saying a deal with P&O was six months away.
He said the P&O deal was urgently required to expand capacity to handle rising container volumes and retain Colombo's position as a hub port, he said.
The port, with a capacity of 1.6 million containers, is expected to handle 1.3 million containers this year, up from just over a million last year, he said.
